justification: Assessment returned INVALID at step 0012 with the same defect as ground truth: the Bellman-Ford loop invariant is stated as an equality, but in-place relaxation within one pass reads already-updated dist values, so dist[u] can be strictly less than the best <=k-edge path length. Its witness (s->u w=10, s->v w=1, v->u w=1; order (s,v),(v,u),(s,u)) checks out by hand: after iteration 1 dist[v]=1, dist[u]=1+1=2, then s->u offers 10 which is not an improvement, so dist[u]=2 while OPT_1(u)=10. Different but valid witness for the identical claim; also identifies the same root cause (tacitly frozen dist values during an iteration) and the same correct weakening to an inequality.
